subject: frog
pitch: A red-eyed tree frog clinging to a leaf. Vivid lime-green skin, blue and cream striped flanks, orange toes with round sticky pads, a creamy white belly, and enormous ruby-red eyes with black slit pupils. It looks a little surprised, as if you just woke it up.
reasoning:
I'm planning to build a single TypeScript module using the SDK, scaling the frog to roughly 6cm body length with legs extended for about 12cm span, positioned standing on a leaf so the model's lowest points touch ground level, treating the leaf as an integrated scenery piece of the design.

I'm sketching the skeleton setup: creating a builder instance named for the red-eyed tree frog, then defining joints starting from a root body joint and building a spine chain from the rear of the body toward the head using a sequence of points.

I'm working through how the chain function resolves parenting—checking whether path weights exist and realizing a root joint needs to exist before the chain can attach to it, since there are no joints yet to anchor to otherwise. Given that complexity, I'm leaning toward building most of the frog's shapes directly with primitive parts rather than relying heavily on chains and sweeps.

I'm sketching out the joint hierarchy for the limbs—hip, knee, ankle, toe for each leg—with the hind legs folded up and the front legs splayed outward to grip the leaf, since the frog needs to look like it's clinging rather than standing freely. I'm also mapping out coordinates for the leaf itself: a flattened elliptical slab sitting near y=0 so the frog's feet rest just above it, working out the point ordering needed to get the surface normal facing upward correctly.

Working out leaf polygon points and slab thickness...

For the frog body, I'm scaling a sphere to create a squashed torso shape sitting slightly above the leaf surface so the belly and limbs appear to cling to it naturally, with toes sinking just enough into the leaf to look grounded without floating.

Now I'm sketching out the joint hierarchy: a root "body" joint, a "head" joint at the neck pivot, and a "jaw" joint for mouth articulation, keeping orientations mostly at default identity rather than complicating with aim vectors. I'm also planning the bulging eyes as spheres protruding from the sides of the head, each with a flattened pupil shape for that classic red-eyed tree frog look.

For the surprised expression, I'm deciding to skip posing the jaw open and instead rely on wide, protruding eyes to convey the look, keeping the rest pose neutral. I'm now sketching the lower jaw as a separate flattened sphere part attached beneath the head.

I'm working out the hind leg structure — hip, knee, and ankle joints positioned so the legs fold with knees pointing outward and forward while the feet tuck back onto the leaf, checking that foot placement stays within the leaf's width at each z-depth. I'm planning to build the legs using capsule geometry between these joints, bound to bones for articulation.

Actually a simpler, more robust approach: build each leg from two capsule segments instead of one smooth tube, with the knee as a shared joint point—capsule from hip to knee with bone hipL, then capsule from knee to ankle with bone kneeL, letting the rounded caps overlap naturally at the joint. I'll add a small sphere at the knee for a bulge, then move on to defining the front legs with shoulder and elbow joints.

I'm planning finger and toe joints as digit chains with pads, then moving to the head and eye placement, and now working through how the belly sphere should overlap the torso so it reads as a visible countershaded patch rather than being hidden inside the body geometry.

Writing paint function for body colors...

Still writing paint logic...

Now I'm thinking about the limbs sharing the lime material while head and torso use the paint texture, and adding details like orange pads on toes, ruby eyes with a slit pupil and a tiny white highlight sphere, plus optional small dark nostrils on the snout.

Working through the head geometry, I'm checking that the eye spheres bulge outside the head's width for a proper frog look, placing a cream lower jaw capsule near the head's underside, and confirming the overall body proportions stay in reasonable ratio once legs are included. Now I'm setting up the front leg capsules running from shoulder to elbow and elbow to wrist.

Planning finger digits...

Chains work well for legs and arms since they give proper joint roles and parent linking automatically, with the tip joint landing at the path's end point. I'm planning to parent toe/finger digits off the ankle and wrist tips, and considering whether chains are really the cleanest way to set up the arm joints versus doing it manually.

For mirroring, I'll loop over both sides with a sign multiplier to flip x-coordinates for left and right. Then for each limb segment I'll build a capsule between the joint positions, rigging it to the correct named bone so the mesh deforms properly with the skeleton.

Now I'm roughing out the frog's hind leg geometry -- placing hip, knee, ankle, and toe joints with folded positions so the legs tuck naturally against the body, then attaching the foot pads to the leaf-shaped body.

Working out digit and finger placement...

Now I'm moving to the head joint hierarchy and eye placement, figuring out sphere surface geometry so the pupil sits correctly embedded on the eye's curved front without exceeding the sphere's radius at that offset.

Still placing head details... nostrils, lower jaw bone setup, and now working out the flank striping—thinking I'll use blue and cream stripes on the flanks with lime as the base body color for the back.

I'm defining a paint function that assigns cream to the belly based on normal direction, flank stripes to the sides, and lime everywhere else, with the leaf texture using a mottled dark-light green pattern.

Now I'm adding leaf details: a thin midrib rod running along the center using a lighter green, and adjusting the leaf's vertical position so its lowest points just barely touch or sink slightly into the floor, staying within the 2% height tolerance.

I'm working through the frog's body geometry on top of the leaf — positioning the front legs' wrists and toe tips so they rest naturally on the leaf surface, setting hind ankle and toe pad placement, and sizing the torso as a scaled sphere attached to the body joint so its underside clears the leaf. I'm also defining the head joint and sphere, checking that the head's bottom aligns just above the torso's top so the two connect smoothly, and noting where the cream belly coloring should blend in based on surface normal direction.

Now I'm placing the eyes and nostrils on the head, sizing the pupils and checking that they bulge outward correctly, then adding a jaw joint with a lower jaw piece sized and positioned to sit just inside the head's front contour.

Working out the shoulder, elbow, and wrist joint positions for the front limb chain, checking that the shoulder sits just at the torso's surface boundary.

Writing capsule limb geometry... Defining the mirrored arm chain and fingers with tip offsets for each digit, mirroring the x-coordinates for left versus right sides.

Now I'm sketching the hind leg chain—hip, knee, and ankle positions forming a bent leg shape toward a foot placed on the leaf, naming the joints and setting their parent-child hierarchy under the body, then building thigh and shin capsules with tapering radii.

I'm defining four hind toe positions radiating outward from the ankle, computing their tip coordinates with a lowered y-value, and planning toe pad placements. Then I'm working out the leaf shape itself as a polygon of x,z points at a fixed slab height, checking that the toe x-position at that z-depth stays within the leaf's width so the foot lands properly on the leaf surface.

I'm sketching the midrib as a rod running along the leaf's length, confirming it sits slightly above the slab surface and uses rigid body-bone weighting since it's attached via a string reference rather than a chain.

Now I'm working out the eye details—glint placement, pupil box dimensions, and material colors for the ruby eyes, black pupil, and white glint—plus deciding on sphere segment counts to keep geometry reasonably low-poly.

I'm laying out the overall code structure: imports, color constants, paint functions for the lime body with cream-and-blue striped flanks, and a mottled green paint for the leaf. Writing skeleton joints...

Continuing to define the chain-based limb skeletons for both arms and legs with mirrored left/right offsets, then adding digit joints, capsule segments, and toe pads for fingers and toes. Writing part geometry...

I'm placing the torso, head, jaw, nostril, eye, pupil, and glint parts with their bone attachments and scale adjustments, then generalizing a digit-building function that creates knuckle-to-tip capsules and pad spheres for each toe and finger, applying mirrored x-offsets based on side. Writing digit placement code...

Now I'm calculating the hind leg joint positions—hip, knee, and ankle—checking that the thigh and shin capsule lengths and radii look proportionate for a frog's folded leg posture.

Finalizing the leaf slab points, midrib rod placement, and eye/pupil/glint parts, then returning the root builder object to complete the model.
